appraisal_events.evidence: « Oh ! mais je vois ce que c'est... Et c'est elle que tu trouves belle ! Mais elle est horrible et elle l'a toujours été »; « je me sentais rougir de honte »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's mother bluntly exposes and mocks his mistaken admiration for Mme Blatin in front of the family, leaving him ashamed.

appraisal_events.evidence: « il faut bien qu'elle soit une espèce de folle... si elle connaît vraiment Odette »; « à cause de Odette qu'elle ne voulait pas connaître »
appraisal_events.explanation: The mother treats acquaintance with Odette as itself suspect and deliberately avoids any reconciliation that would involve knowing her, keeping Odette at a social remove.

status_effects.explanation: He is locally embarrassed and diminished when his mother mocks and corrects his misplaced admiration in front of the family.
The mother's suspicion of association with her and her refusal to acknowledge her keep Odette outside the family's valued social circle.

ambiguities: The mother's remark that acquaintance with Odette marks Mme Blatin as 'une espèce de folle' primarily characterizes Mme Blatin (not a candidate); the implied discredit of Odette is inferred rather than stated outright, so this reading carries moderate uncertainty.
